title: A novel approach to minimize the false negative COVID-19 diagnosis by inclusion of specific cell markers and multiple sample collection
author: Husain

steps.title: Day‑1 sample collection and pooling
steps.instruction: Collect a nasopharyngeal (NP) swab and an oropharyngeal (OP) swab from the patient, place each swab into Virus Transport Media (VTM), then combine the two VTM tubes into a single tube.

substeps.instruction: Collect NP swab and insert into VTM.
Collect OP swab and insert into VTM.
Mix the two VTM tubes to create a pooled Day‑1 sample.

steps.title: Extract RNA from Day‑1 pool
steps.instruction: Perform RNA extraction on the pooled Day‑1 VTM to obtain RNA pool‑A, following the extraction kit’s standard protocol.

steps.title: Day‑3 sample collection and pooling
steps.instruction: Two days later (Day‑3), repeat the NP and OP swab collection, place each swab into VTM, and combine the two VTM tubes into a single tube.

substeps.instruction: Collect NP swab and insert into VTM.
Collect OP swab and insert into VTM.
Mix the two VTM tubes to create a pooled Day‑3 sample.

steps.title: Extract RNA from Day‑3 pool
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the pooled Day‑3 VTM to obtain RNA pool‑B, using the same extraction method as for Day‑1.

steps.title: Combine RNA pools
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of RNA pool‑A and RNA pool‑B to generate a combined RNA template for downstream RT‑PCR.

steps.title: Set up RT‑PCR with controls
steps.instruction: Prepare the RT‑PCR reaction using the combined RNA as template and include primers for SARS‑CoV‑2 E gene and RdRp, an external RNA spike‑in added during extraction, RNase P primers, and primers for the three cell‑type markers (goblet cell, type‑II pneumocyte, intestinal enterocyte).

substeps.instruction: Add pooled RNA template to the RT‑PCR master mix.
Add primer sets for viral E gene and RdRp.
Add RNase P primer set (RNA quality control).
Add primer sets for goblet cell, type‑II pneumocyte, and intestinal enterocyte markers.

steps.title: Run RT‑PCR and analyze
steps.instruction: Run the RT‑PCR under the cycling conditions recommended by the kit, then examine amplification curves: viral gene amplification indicates a positive result; amplification of any cell‑type marker with no viral signal indicates a true negative; absence of cell‑type marker amplification suggests a sampling or extraction failure.

steps.title: Document detection probabilities
steps.instruction: Record the expected detection probabilities for reference: 66 % for nasal (NP/OP) samples and 33 % for pharyngeal samples.
